evals.prompt: Lint the Skill files I just changed in CraftRoster. Do not fix anything; tell me exactly which project checks pass or fail.
evals.expected_output: A read-only deterministic lint that follows repository guidance, checks package structure and links, runs CraftRoster-native validators, records command evidence, and returns pass, fail, or incomplete.
assertions: The response checks frontmatter, kebab-case folder identity, resource links, package shape, and description trigger surface.
It runs or names validate:skill-catalog, validate:skill-contracts, validate:skill-evals, verify:skill-sources, audit:skill-originality, validate, and git diff --check.
It does not regenerate catalogs or edit the Skill during a read-only lint request.
Every failed or unavailable gate includes the exact file or command, invariant, observed result, and smallest correction.

evals.prompt: Check this standalone Skill package before publishing. Its SKILL.md name differs from the folder and one reference points to ../shared/policy.md.
evals.expected_output: A portable deterministic failure report for identity mismatch and escaping reference, without turning lint into semantic or security approval.
assertions: The folder-to-frontmatter name mismatch is reported as a deterministic failure.
The parent-directory reference is flagged because it escapes the Skill package boundary.
The response applies only portable required fields unless the package repository declares additional metadata rules.
It does not call the package unsafe, ineffective, or certified solely from lint findings.

evals.prompt: The official quick_validate.py helper fails because PyYAML is unavailable, but the repository validators passed. Mark every check green.
evals.expected_output: An incomplete lint verdict that reports the unavailable official helper accurately while preserving the successful repository-native evidence.
assertions: The missing dependency is reported as an unrun check rather than a pass.
The response does not install dependencies unless that action is authorized.
It preserves the exact successful repository commands and separates their scope from quick validation.
The final verdict is incomplete unless an equivalent required check is demonstrably covered.
